text: Two studies show non-coding 3'UTRs modulate microRNA function. In mouse breast carcinoma 4T1 cells, the versican 3'UTR antagonizes miR-199a-3p, lowering its levels; miR-199a-3p and miR-144 target cell-cycle regulator Rb1, while miR-144 and miR-136 target PTEN. By binding these miRNAs, the 3'UTR freed Rb1 and PTEN mRNAs for translation, up-regulating both synergistically in vitro and in vivo. Cells transfected with the 3'UTR formed smaller tumors than controls, implicating miRNA degradation in tumorigenesis. Separately, the ~1.7 kb spliced, highly abundant murine cytomegalovirus m169 transcript mediates rapid, mutual degradation of cellular miR-27a/b during lytic infection via a single optimized miRNA binding site in its 3'-UTR. Expressing only the m169 3'-UTR from an adenoviral vector sufficed; degradation involved 3'-tailing and trimming. Three mutant viruses unable to target miR-27a/b lost efficiency in vivo.
